analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md: the "Last updated" date (line 3) and a paragraph about CI run-isolation regressions (head lines ~2192-2197). The supplied head excerpts (lines 451-1359) are unchanged surrounding documentation. I examined them against the canonical threat model, including T-041 (prefix-cache SSD), TB-011 (App Attest), TB-012 (add-on hold) and the endpoint-resumption and logout tests.

The documentation describes test procedures only. It introduces no code, configuration, endpoint, key handling, authorization or cache-policy change. The test-recipe guidance on isolated key namespaces and never using production cache roots or keys is consistent with the T-041 posture and the retained mitigations. No threat-model assumption is invalidated. The run-isolation test text describes CI runner label selection and does not alter provider, coordinator or attestation behavior.

The patch hunk's changed lines (about 2192-2197) fall outside the supplied text units, so I could only evaluate that hunk from the patch excerpt. It is descriptive prose about CI label routing and tests. I saw no security regression, new attack surface or threat-model gap. The CI runner label routing implementation itself was not supplied, so its actual isolation behavior is unverified. That is a coverage limit, not a finding.
